problem: Determine the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}-4}{{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}}.$

choices.value: The function has no vertical asymptotes

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Vertical Asymptotes With Common Factors in the Numerator and Denominator
examples.worked_solution:
To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the numerator and denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}-6x+8} \\  & =\frac{x-2}{(x-2)(x-4)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x-2}}{\cancel{(x-2)}(x-4)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
x - 4 = 0
$$

This gives the solution $x = 4.$ Therefore, $x = 4$ is the only vertical asymptote.

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Adding both fractions and then factoring the numerator and denominator, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{1}{x+5} \\  & =\frac{2(x+5)+(x-1)}{(x-1)(x+5)} \\  & =\frac{2x+10+x-1}{(x-1)(x+5)} \\  & =\frac{3x+9}{(x-1)(x+5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)(x+5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the two solutions $x=-5$ and $x=1.$ 

Therefore, in ascending order, the equations of the vertical asymptotes are $x=-5$ and $x=1.$
